clue.text: Naturalist sketch almost having repelled artist

indicators.note: repelled says the artist's two letters are pushed back the other way round
almost says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a sketch is a drawing
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A wildlife expert's sketch is nearly done, having driven off some painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' looks like a verb, but it is a noun; 'almost' drops the final letter and 'having repelled' turns the artist's letters round where they sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin, the Victorian scientist of the Beagle voyage, is the most famous naturalist.

clue.text: Guarding ostrich, guarding dog

indicators.note: the outer words guard what lies within, so the letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An animal watches over a big bird, protecting a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild dog of Australia, a feral canine.

clue.text: Instrument missing middle note? Choose again

indicators.note: missing says the note is taken out

parts.note: a recorder is a wind instrument
middle C is the note at the centre of the piano keyboard

explanation.surface: A wind instrument lacks a central note, so pick another one.
explanation.definitionFit: To order again means making a fresh request or selection.

clue.text: Safe place for eggs on island hill

parts.note: in can mean on, as in 'in the subject of'
Cuba is a Caribbean island
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A secure nest for eggs sits on a hill on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmed apparatus where eggs are hatched under controlled conditions.

clue.text: Small German greeting a female informally

parts.note: Heil is a German word of salute

explanation.surface: A little German man says hello to a woman in a casual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a girl or woman, fitting the puzzle's Antipodean theme.

clue.text: Devise mark with intersecting lines

definitions.meaning: to devise is to plot or concoct a scheme

explanation.surface: Plan to draw a grid of crossed lines.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means to plot a scheme; another means to shade a drawing with fine parallel strokes.

clue.text: Not quite right in previous performance

parts.note: ex means former, previous
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Something was a little off in an earlier show.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise or slightly wrong, lacking exactness.

clue.text: Southern Climes article with hints about poetry

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about says the hints go around the poem

parts.note: tips are hints
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A travel piece on warm southern lands includes advice on verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The far side of the globe from Britain, chiefly Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Bill might be ready for a singalong

definitions.meaning: a bill is a statement of charges

definitions.text: might be ready for a singalong
definitions.meaning: read as two words, the answer says a singer is warmed up and in good voice

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill could be all set for a group sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill for goods supplied is the commercial document sent to a customer for payment.

clue.text: Threw up on street. Blimey!

indicators.note: up here means stirred or disordered, so the letters of threw are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vomited in the road, prompting a cry of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the anagram signal on 'Threw'; the abbreviation for street goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise; this one is Australian and British slang, a corruption of God's truth.

clue.text: One with a pouch to cook pilau under ruins

indicators.note: in a down clue under places the cooked rice below the ruins piece

parts.note: mars means spoils or ruins

indicators.note: to cook means to fiddle or rework, so the letters of pilau are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature with a pocket cooks rice dish among old ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos and their relatives carry their young in a pouch.

clue.text: Agent has individual book every surfing hotspot

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional secret agent
I is the single person, one individual
each means every

explanation.surface: A spy owns a personal copy of every volume.
explanation.definitionFit: This Sydney shoreline is one of the world's best-known places to ride waves.

clue.text: Insects originally exterminated snakes

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter, which is wiped out

parts.note: wasps are stinging insects

explanation.surface: Bugs were wiped out at first, leaving serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: These are venomous snakes, like the Egyptian cobra Cleopatra used.

clue.text: Most awful meat reported by some

indicators.note: reported says the word is spoken; by some because only some accents make the two match

parts.note: wurst is German sausage, a meat

explanation.surface: Some people say the meat was dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bad: poorest in quality, the most dreadful.

clue.text: Team of leaderless infants lifting barrier

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue says the barrier goes on top of the rest

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: leaderless says the first letter goes

parts.note: babies are infants

explanation.surface: Some side of babies with no guide is raising a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian national rugby union side is nicknamed after a small kangaroo-like animal.

clue.text: Criminal is led out in isolation

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is taken out to be kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone and apart from others is solitariness, exactly what isolation describes.

clue.text: Pal craned awkwardly to see club worker

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend stretched their neck clumsily to see someone at a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic dancer working in a strip club performs close to a customer.

clue.text: Fitting vocal work after hollow choral bilge

indicators.note: after puts the fitting and vocal pieces behind the hollowed word
hollow says the word is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: apt means fitting
rap is a spoken musical form

explanation.surface: A suitable song follows some empty choir music that is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for nonsense, and so is empty showy talk of this kind.

clue.text: Humourless fellow meets expert in school

indicators.note: in places these two pieces inside the school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A dour man meets a top teacher at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stern, disapproving expression with no sense of fun.

clue.text: Couples pop by tax department in USA

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, as is pa
the IRS is the Internal Revenue Service

explanation.surface: Couples pass by the American tax office.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples and twosomes are sets of two people or things.

clue.text: From Spain maybe tailless goat fled across Italy

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an ibex is a wild mountain goat

indicators.note: across says the fleeing goes around Italy's letter

parts.note: ran means fled
I is the international car code for Italy

explanation.surface: A goat without a tail ran away across Italy, possibly from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal; Spain is one example, hence maybe.

clue.text: Head left periodically for a swift one?

indicators.note: periodically picks letters at regular intervals, here the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: The boss kept leaving now and then for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'swift one' is a quick drink; in Britain a half is a half-pint of beer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-pint of beer is a small drink, the sort you have when popping in quickly.

clue.text: 10 creatures from lake a boar's ravaged

indicators.note: ravaged suggests being torn apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Animals came from a lake that a boar had wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the answer at 10 down, MARSUPIAL: these animals are pouched.
explanation.definitionFit: These tree-dwelling Australian animals carry young in a pouch, so they are pouched creatures.

clue.text: Boy finally stops dancing like Dannii's sister?

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so that letter sits inside the rearranged ones
dancing says the letters of like move about into a new order
finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boy at last stops jigging about like a famous pop star's sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dannii Minogue's sister is the Australian pop singer; the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Circular piece of wood Norwegian put up

indicators.note: put up says the hidden letters are read backwards
of says the letters come out of the following words, sitting across their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A round item is made of Scandinavian timber, put up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no hidden-word signal; 'of' supplies it, the letters coming from 'wood Norwegian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical movement whose main theme keeps returning, like going round in a circle.

clue.text: 1000mm3 found in car? Blow into this

indicators.note: found in puts the measurement inside the car

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car model
a thousand cubic millimetres is one cubic centimetre, I CC

explanation.surface: A small volume turned up in a vehicle; give it a puff.
explanation.definitionFit: A small high-pitched flute, a wind instrument played by blowing across its hole.

clue.text: Animal character from Greece captured by Dame

indicators.note: captured by puts the letter inside the dame's name

parts.note: Dame Edna Everage is Barry Humphries' Australian stage character
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure is caught by a grande dame.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea, an egg-laying mammal.

clue.text: City strategy damn easy — all to be evacuated

indicators.note: evacuated says each word is emptied, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An urban plan says every resident must be cleared out, which is no easy matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's largest urban centre, capital of New South Wales.

clue.text: Imbecile split on doctor working

indicators.note: on puts the split piece after the doctor and working pieces

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
split is slang for leave, go

explanation.surface: A fool divided over a medic at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a fool or idiot, from an awkward-looking bird.
